deceased fell down and succumbed to grievous injuries on the way to the hospital.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the Petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale, healthy and was aged about 44 years and he was working as a Driver at Dayal Logistics, Karnal - 132001 and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners became dark,
miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569.
In this regard, criminal case was registered by Nelamangala Traffic Police against him, in Crime No.61/2024 on the basis of the first information received by one Narayanaswamy in this regard.
As such, the Respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence,
this petition.
5. After service of the notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2/Insurance company appeared through it's Counsel and filed written statement.

6. The Respondent No.2 in the written statement denied about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569 as on the date of the accident, however restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is contended that the driver of offending vehicle does not posses valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of the accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied the involvement of the offending in the alleged accident and said vehicle is falsely implicated in the accident in order to get compensation.

The respondent took specific contention that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself, as he was riding his motor cycle wearing helmet and without giving any signal or indication all of a sudden stopped his vehicle in the middle of the road, due to which he lost control and fell on the road due to skid and fall.
It is also contended that the deceased does not posses valid D.L on the date of the accident.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated.

And stated that, neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) and S.158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
It is also denied the age, avocation, income of the deceased and also relationship with the petitioners.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition, against the respondent No.2.
7.

sentences.text: ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that Shri.Kumar .M. died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 16-02-2024 at about 2- 45 a.m.

Opp. Indian Oil Petrol bunk, Bengaluru - Tumkur NH-48 road, Hosanijagal, Nelamangala Taluk, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
4) What order or award?

On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Narayanaswamy K., the S.H.O. of Nelamangala Traffic Police has registered the case against the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 304(A) of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against one Thippeswamy A. who being the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569 alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.

Though, the Respondent No.2 has taken specific contention that the offending vehicle is not involved in the alleged accident, the Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence and also not placed any evidence to show that, the offending vehicle is not involved in the accident.

18. After careful scrutiny of Police documents i.e., FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch,
Inquest report, P.M. report, Notices U/sec.133 of IMV Act, and replies to the said notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, IMV report and Charge sheet, and in the light of the evidence placed by Petitioner, I am of the view that, the Petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.
Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569 and in the said accident,
Sri .Kumar M., succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the Petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since it is the death case, the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P13 to Ex.P16 and Ex.P18 Aadhar cards of the Petitioners and the deceased, which have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
21. In the case on hand, no doubt the major sons of Kumar .M. filed this claim petition.
According to them, they were dependents to the deceased petitioner during his lifetime.

PW.1 deposed in his croo examination that, Petitioner No.1 is his mother and she is Housewife, Petitioner No.3 and 4 are his sisters and they are married and residing in their husband's house separately.
Here, it is necessary discuss the point that, whether major children are fully dependent upon deceased their father.

All the children, one or the other way dependents to their parents, whether they are minors or majors,
married or unmarried.
But the percentage of dependency may be varied from one person to another person.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the parents.
After the marriage of the children, the percentage of dependency is less on the parents, if compare with the minor children.

22. In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major children, they could have dependents to their parents not only economically, but in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the Petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their father during his lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.

In this regard, I have relied the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court (DB), in National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others, which is stated that as under:-
"A major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Vehicle Act.

sentences.text: In this case, by referring the case of Manjuri Bera, stated that, even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant if he was a legal representative will be entitled to compensation.

Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation, and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application, irrespective of the fact, whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

23. The petitioners herein, to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident,
they have produced Ex.P13 notarized copy of the Aadhaar card of the deceased.
It discloses that the date of birth of the deceased as 03-02-1979.
On perusal of P.M. report marked at Ex.P6, age of the deceased was mentioned as 45 years.
The said document remained unquestioned by the other side.
Hence, it is safely to be considered that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged about 45 years.
For his age, multiplier '14' is applicable as per the ratio laid down in "Sarala Verma" Case.

In connection with the work of the deceased in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing Driver job in Dayal Logistics and used to earn income of Rs.40,000/- per month.
But in support of definite income of the deceased, there is no iota of documents and the petitioners have not examined the employer of the deceased.

In such a situation,
as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.
25. Another point to be taken into consideration herein that, as per the petition, 4 persons were depending on the earning of the deceased.
In this regard, about the deduction of the personal and living expenses is concerned, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.
26. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National
Insurance
Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,

wherein it was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.
And 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

27. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "Where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd ) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5th) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
28. In the light of the above proposition in the case on hand, there are 4 persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
29. In the present case, deceased was aged about 45 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "14" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.

Co. ltd., V/s Gummanna and others., in MFA.No.8625/2023 (MV-D) dt: 04-07-2024 order passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru, wherein the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka, held that the compensation granted under the head loss of future prospectus is with regard to probable income tobe received in the future and as such, there is no requirement to grant interest on the award amount towards future prospectus.

consortium, and funeral expenses.
In this case, the Petitioner No.2 to 4 are children of deceased person and are entitled for compensation under the head parental consortium.
33. In this regard, it is relevant to rely the case of National Insurance Company Limited.
V/s Pranay Sethi and others, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

37. Liability:-
As per the Petition, the Respondent No.1 is the RC Owner & Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569.
As already discussed in the issue no.1 and it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further the Respondent No.2 is being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the Petitioner.
Accordingly the issue No.2 answered in the Affirmative and Isssue No.3 answered partly in the Affirmative.
38. Issue No.4:

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,29,000/- along with the interest at the rate of 6% p.m. (excluding compensation awarded under the head future Prospectus) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 60%, the Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for the share of 10% each.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- for the death of Kumar M. in a road traffic accident.
It is contended that the driver of offending vehicle does not posses valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of the accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
The respondent took specific contention that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself, as he was riding his motor cycle wearing helmet and without giving any signal or indication all of a sudden stopped his vehicle in the middle of the road, due to which he lost control and fell on the road due to skid and fall.
opennyai_summary.issue:

2) Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate? from whom?
4) What order or award?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against one Thippeswamy A. who being the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569 alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.
17.
Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569 and in the said accident,
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the Petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since it is the death case, the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the parents.
After the marriage of the children, the percentage of dependency is less on the parents, if compare with the minor children.
22. In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major children, they could have dependents to their parents not only economically, but in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the Petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their father during his lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.
In this regard, I have relied the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court (DB), in National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others, which is stated that as under:-
"A major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Vehicle Act.
23. The petitioners herein, to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident,
they have produced Ex.P13 notarized copy of the Aadhaar card of the deceased.
On perusal of P.M. report marked at Ex.P6, age of the deceased was mentioned as 45 years.
Pushpa Kumar vs Santhosh Kumar P on 9 December, 2024
But in support of definite income of the deceased, there is no iota of documents and the petitioners have not examined the employer of the deceased.
In such a situation,
as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.
Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
27. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "Where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd ) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5th) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
29. In the present case, deceased was aged about 45 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "14" is applicable.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
opennyai_summary.decision:
a) Income of the deceased is taken at Rs. 16,000-00 b) Add the future prospectus of Rs. 20,000-00 Rs.16,000/-+4,000/- (25%)
c) Deduction towards personal expenses: Rs. 15,000-00 Rs.20000/- - Rs.5000/- (1/4th )
Therefore this tribunal took the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-, which comes as under:-
Rs.15,000 X 12 X 14 = Rs.25,20,000/- Hence, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,20,000/- under the head loss of dependency.
30.
And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads:-
Compensation heads Compensation Amount Towards loss of Rs.18,90,000-00 dependency Towards future prospectus Rs.6,30,000-00 (25%)
Towards loss of Rs.
1,76,000-00 consortium Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00 Towards funeral & Rs.
16,500-00 obsequies ceremony expenses Total Rs.27,29,000-00 36.
Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.27,29,000/-
along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA.No.103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018. And MFA.No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020 from the date of petition till its realization.
(excluding the compensation awarded under the dead future Prospectus).
37. Liability:-
As per the Petition, the Respondent No.1 is the RC Owner & Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/AJ-7569.
As already discussed in the issue no.1 and it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further the Respondent No.2 is being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the Petitioner.
Accordingly the issue No.2 answered in the Affirmative and Isssue No.3 answered partly in the Affirmative.
38. Issue No.4:
In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,29,000/- along with the interest at the rate of 6% p.m. (excluding compensation awarded under the head future Prospectus) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 60%, the Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for the share of 10% each.
Pushpa Kumar vs Santhosh Kumar P on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146974848/
9
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of Petitioner No.1, shall deposit 40% of her share in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released in favour of Petitioner No.1 through due process of law.
After deposit, entire share compensation amount of 10% each together with interest of Petitioner No.2 to 4 shall be released to them through due process of law.
[ Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
